terms.gloss: a bow; an arc, an arch; the rainbow
evidence: Col. 5.2.9: Sī autem minus quam sēmicirculus erit, arcum sīc mētiēmur
Col. 5.2.1: aut etiam sēmicirculī, vel arcūs … fōrmam
terms.comment: The bow, and so anything bent like one: an arch, the rainbow, and in Columella a piece of a circle smaller than a semicircle.

terms.register: vōx plērumque poētica: Ov.; in ōrātiōne solūtā Plin. Ep.
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: not before Augustus, perhaps first in Ovid.

terms.gloss: a curve, a curvature; a vault
evidence: Col. 5.2.8: curvātūrae autem lātitūdō pedēs LXX
terms.comment: The technical writers’ word for the bend of a line or a vault.

phrases.latin: Nōn rēctam līneam dūxistī, sed curvam: arcus est, ut pluvius.
phrases.english: You didn’t draw a straight line, but a curved one: it’s an arc, like a rainbow.

phrases.latin: quālis ab imbre solent percussīs sōlibus arcus īnficere ingentī longum curvāmine caelum
phrases.english: as, after rain, when the sunlight strikes it, the rainbow paints the long sky with its huge curve

phrases.latin: Sī autem minus quam sēmicirculus erit, arcum sīc mētiēmur.
phrases.english: But if it is less than a semicircle, we shall measure the arc like this.

sources: Lewis & Short: arcus · Lewis & Short: curvamen · Lewis & Short: curvatura
